claim: Let \(\nu^k\) be uniform on \(\{-k+1,-k+3,\ldots,k-1\}\), and let \(T(\alpha)\) be the extremal mixture defined in Juškevičius (2024, Conjecture 6.1). For three independent summands with parameters \((\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=(1/20,1/20,1/10)\), the variance-matched common parameter is \(\alpha=619/10710\), but \(\mathcal Q_2(\sum_{i=1}^3T(\alpha_i))=7/160>219116707/5055477000=\mathcal Q_2(\sum_{i=1}^3T(\alpha))\); hence the conjectured variance-matched equalization inequality is false.
integrity: The first public date is the arXiv v1 submission date, not the later journal date.
All probabilities and variances in the claim are computed with exact rational arithmetic.
scientific_limitations: The result is one finite exact counterexample to Conjecture 6.1, not a classification of all parameters.
The strict difference is small but exact: \(8241647/20221908000\).
The exact arithmetic verifies the stated finite support only; no replacement inequality is claimed.
title: A finite exact counterexample to variance-matched concentration equalization
